children: Alphabet's
Waymo is taking its autonomous ride-hailing business into Canada, signing a binding framework to launch
fully autonomous service in Toronto in 2028
The move marks another important geographic expansion for Waymo as Alphabet looks to turn years of autonomous-driving investment into a broader commercial transportation network.
Waymo plans to begin
manual mapping and validation drives
around Toronto in the near term, laying the groundwork for the eventual driverless rollout.
The company will work with Toronto-based
Element Fleet Management
to handle end-to-end fleet services.
Waymo also expects the expansion to create
hundreds of jobs over time
across fleet maintenance, validation driving, customer service and operations.

Expanding into Canada marks an important milestone in Waymo's global journey, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana said, adding that Waymo wants to contribute to safer streets and more accessible transportation in Toronto.
The move builds on Waymo's existing Canadian relationships.
The
Canada Pension Plan Investment Board
has been a long-term investor in the autonomous-driving company, while Canadian auto supplier Magna International
is already a manufacturing partner.

The planned Toronto launch also shows how Waymo is beginning to move beyond proving that autonomous vehicles work toward proving that the business can be replicated across different cities, regulations and operating environments.
Investor Takeaway
I think the important part of the Toronto announcement is not simply that Waymo is entering another city.
It is that Alphabet is beginning to test whether Waymo can become a
repeatable international platform

Toronto brings different weather, regulation and operating conditions than many of Waymo's existing markets, making the expansion a potentially important test of how easily its autonomous-driving technology can scale.
The 2028 target also gives Waymo considerable time for mapping, regulatory work and fleet preparation before carrying paying passengers without drivers.
For Alphabet investors, the key things to watch are
fleet size, regulatory approvals, ride volumes, geographic expansion and whether Waymo can lower the cost of operating each vehicle as scale increases
If Toronto succeeds, Canada could become another launchpad for broader international expansion rather than a one-city experiment.

title: Google Parent Alphabet Has a Big Surprise for Waymo
